reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports that redox potential governs oxidation and causes compositional inversion in the baseline alloy. E2 shows that partial Mn substitution with a lower redox potential element (Al) alters the oxide layer, but provides no evidence for higher redox potential dopants (Mo/W) or their predicted effect. E3 discusses oxidation resistance in a different alloy system (FeNiCuAl-based) and does not address the proposed mechanism. Thus, the core premise that a higher redox potential dopant will retard oxidation and stabilize the scale is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: In equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn, oxidation kinetics are governed by redox potential, causing compositional inversion at the oxide/alloy interface.
Substituting Mn with a higher redox potential element (Mo or W) will preferentially resist oxidation and influence early oxide nucleation.
This substitution will create a modified oxide scale with reduced compositional inversion and a more protective, stable film.
The modified scale will lower diffusion of oxygen and metal cations, slowing overall oxidation kinetics.
The effect is achievable with small dopant concentrations that preserve phase stability.
